intro: Each image is built through a deliberate decision. The set establishes a story, the lighting directs attention to a garment, or two exposures put different spaces in one frame.
alt: Three photographs of the heroine in a surreal blue set, a wine-red fashion studio and an exposure layered with trees and architecture.

variants.name: staged photography
variants.look: The arranged set and blue light put an everyday figure inside an improbable scene.
variants.history: Staged photographers adapt tools from the theater and studio, arranging subjects, props and lighting before taking the picture.
variants.when: Use a constructed set to make a portrait carry a specific story.
variants.why: The set gives even the smallest object a part to play in the scene.

source.label: Philadelphia Museum of Art | Staged studio photographs

variants.name: fashion photography
variants.look: Hard light and a long pose bring out the fit and seams of the dress.
variants.history: Fashion photographers have worked with magazines and designers to turn garments into editorial pictures. Studio photographers such as Irving Penn made clothing central to the frame.
variants.when: Show the design and silhouette of an outfit as worn.
variants.why: Directional light and pose reveal construction, fabric and motion together.

variants.name: double exposure
variants.look: Branches and building lines appear across the head and jacket while both subjects remain discernible.
variants.history: Twentieth-century experimental photographers explored superimposition and repeated exposure, often to connect subjects that never occupied the same physical space.
variants.when: Tie a portrait to a second image that represents a place or a memory.
variants.why: The overlapping areas let parts of each subject alter the meaning of the other.

prompt: Create wide 3-panel triptych, three independently composed equal-width panels side by side, hard splits at thirds. Repeat this original character in each distinct lens-made photographic idiom. Please produce a wide 3-column triptych of equally large vertical artwork panels meeting at straight vertical splits one-third and two-thirds. Use the attached illustration only as subject character reference. 30-year-old attractive ash-blonde woman with tidy low bun, black rectangular eyeglasses clearly visible in every panel, tailored charcoal knee-length business dress under fitted blazer, signature white coffee mug with small four-color windowpane mark and plain blue lanyard with a blank badge. Never reproduce the card border or typography. The artwork techniques differ dramatically. Put nothing that crosses the splits. No letters, words, numerals or panel labels anywhere. LEFT: staged cinematic photograph, carefully arranged surreal scene of woman holding her cup against overturned furniture, controlled blue spotlights and theater-like set. CENTER: fashion editorial photograph, blazer and fitted business dress photographed impeccably in a tall pose, angled hard magazine light and a rare burgundy set. RIGHT: actual photographic-style double exposure, her glasses and blonde low bun clearly visible over a second exposure of office facade and trees, cool silver-blue palette.
